title: The Call Desk
subtitle: Claude vs. the networks · election night 2026

rule.headline: A race is called only at 99.5% confidence or more.
rule.text: Senate and governor polling averages have historically missed by about five points on average, so a 99.5% (2.6σ) call on polls alone needs a lead of 13 points or more. None of these ten races has one, so the first calls will come from the returns: a race is called when the outstanding vote, at any plausible composition, cannot close the gap. Nothing is called before a state's polls close. Every call carries its timestamp; a wrong call is withdrawn in public and stays in the log.
rule.scoring: Scored against the Associated Press: a call counts when AP later calls the same winner. The AP column shows AP's own call and time as recorded by the Election Desk.

races.name: Georgia Senate
races.note: A 9-point lead is short of the 13 the rule needs. Georgia counts its early vote first, so the first drops will run Democratic; the test is the Election Day vote in the Atlanta exurbs. A majority is required, or it goes to a December runoff.

races.name: Georgia Governor

pollAvg.src: Election Desk mean of 5 polls, Oct. 12–Nov. 2

races.note: The closest race on the board: Research Co. had Bottoms +1, InsiderAdvantage a tie. A runoff is live if nobody clears 50%.

races.name: South Carolina Senate

pollAvg.src: Election Desk mean of 7 polls; PollCheck final average Graham +1.1

races.note: A state Trump carried by 18. If Andrews is within a few points as the Upstate reports, the polls were right and this goes late.

races.name: Ohio Senate (special)

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 1; RealClearPolling has Husted +1

races.note: The averages disagree most here. Ohio reports early and absentee first; watch the margin in Franklin, Cuyahoga and Hamilton against 2024, then the Election Day vote in the rest of the state.

races.name: North Carolina Senate
races.note: Closest to the 13-point line. North Carolina's early vote reports within minutes of 7:30; if Cooper's early-vote margin matches the polls this can be called early.

races.name: Maine Senate

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 2; Silver Bulletin D +3.9

races.note: Collins has beaten her polls before. Maine counts by town and slowly; ranked-choice tabulation only if nobody reaches 50%.

races.name: Texas Senate

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 2; Silver Bulletin D +3.3

races.note: Texas reports its early vote in one large drop around 8 p.m. ET; Election Day votes follow county by county. Most of the state closes at 8, El Paso at 9.

races.name: Michigan Senate
races.note: Michigan now pre-processes mail ballots, so the count is faster than 2020. Wayne and Oakland are the keys; the Upper Peninsula closes at 9.

races.name: Iowa Senate

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 1; Silver Bulletin D +1.1

races.note: A coin flip in the polls. Iowa counts fast; the call will come from the full count, not a projection.

races.name: Kansas Senate
races.note: No Democrat has won a Kansas Senate race since 1932. Johnson County (Kansas City suburbs) decides it; the rural vote reports late.

log.text: 6:03 p.m. ET: Board set. Ten races, calls so far: 0. Nothing has closed, and none of the ten clears a 99.5% bar on polling alone. First results check at 7:40 p.m., then hourly.
